```text
Log a purchase in the local currency and see it in your home currency right away, even offline. Optional daily limit, categories, trips, widget and Apple Watch. Data stays on your iPhone, no account. Free: 1 trip, 3 expenses. One payment unlocks the rest.
```

## Maker 首則留言（發布後立刻貼）

```text
Hi Product Hunt, I'm Guan Feng, a solo iOS developer in Taiwan, and I made G+Money Lite.

The problem I kept having on trips: standing at a counter, looking at a price in yen or won, doing mental maths while a queue forms behind me. And at night I never knew how much I'd actually spent that day, because cash and card were mixed.

So the app does one thing: you log a purchase in the local currency and it shows you the amount in your home currency right away.

A few details I tried to get right:
• Rates refresh when you open the app (about every 6 hours), or you can type in the rate you actually got at the exchange counter.
• No signal (subway, flight, roaming off)? It converts with the last saved rate.
• The automatic rate is a mid-market reference rate, so your card statement can differ a little. I'd rather say that up front.
• Optional daily limit, categories, trips, filters, backup & restore, a widget and an Apple Watch app.
• Everything stays on your iPhone. There's no account and no tracking.
• The interface comes in 50 languages and you can switch inside the app, which helps when the person you travel with reads a different language.

About pricing, honestly: the free version includes rates, budget and the summary, but only 1 trip and 3 expenses, so it's a test drive. One payment unlocks unlimited trips and expenses. There's no subscription.

I'd really like to hear:
1. When you travel, do you log cash and card spending separately, or together?
2. What would make you keep a trip log going past day one?

I'll be here all day answering questions.
```

## 當天回覆備用句（照實回答，不誇大）

- **"Is the rate the same as my card?"** → No. The automatic rate is a mid-market reference. If you want it to match what you actually paid, set a manual rate. Your card statement is the final number.
- **"Android?"** → iPhone only for now (with a widget and an Apple Watch app). I'd rather not promise a date I can't keep.
- **"Why not a subscription?"** → It's a small, offline tool. One payment felt fair for that.
- **"Where is my data?"** → On your device only. No account. Rates come from a public exchange-rate service.
- **"Can I export?"** → There's backup & restore (expenses, rates, categories and settings). If you need a specific export format, tell me what you'd use it for.
